note: Trace form (research/trace-harness.md) for L05: the static twins, served by scripts/trace.sh. Each soak sends one request many times, each with a key of its own ($i), one at a time at most 50 a second, and reads the twin's heap after a full collection (node --expose-gc) before and at each count. Judged on each twin alone, by the rule a real project gets with no twin to compare against: the least-squares slope of the heap over the points from each soak's first count on, which the counts put past every bound the clean twin sets (search: 1,000 entries; recent orders: 100; suggestions: 500; checkout replies: 500), is memory kept per request (STB-05) when it is at least 512 bytes a request with a fit of R² 0.9 or better. A poorer fit is the collector's noise, whatever the slope (CI run 44666936253: 45 and 97 bytes a request at R² 0.22 and 0.06, reported under the earlier twin-against-twin rule). Not soaked: POST /login (L05-3), whose clean twin is bounded at 100,000 sessions, more than a trace sends, so it is confirmed statically and by the load soak; PUT /rates/:pair (d5, d6), whose entries a timer removes after an hour in both twins. defects are what the planted twin must report and the clean twin must not; every other soak is a decoy, in both twins. POST /orders (L05-2) is an expected miss: the planted twin keeps about 83 to 128 bytes an order, under the 512-byte floor, so it stays as the hard case below it; POST /checkout (L05-4), an idempotency store that keeps each cart, is the leak above the floor that must be caught.
